newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post second straight record finish.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post second straight record finish.

text.p: Toronto stocks hit new highs for a second straight session on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's gains after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged.
The TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 22.91 points to 5322.57, a new closing and intraday record.

"A significant number of portfolio managers were sitting on their money, fearful of an increase in interest rates. That did not happen," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.
Toronto outperformed the Dow Jones average, which gained 3.3 points on the day.
Trading on Canada's biggest stock market was brisk with volume of 88.5 million shares worth C$1.3 billion (US$951 million).
Katzin said the current interest rate picture is positive for rate-sensitive stocks, which attracted many buyers today.
The Fed's decision against raising U.S. rates has renewed speculation that the Bank of Canada may have room to cut Canadian interest rates.
Toronto's financial services group added 50 points, leading nine of 14 sectors higher.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 477 to 414 with 309 issues unchanged.
* Among heavy traders, Bank of Montreal rose 0.35 to 37.35 on 1.4 million shares. Royal Bank of Canada gained 1.35 to 39.70 on 1.1 million shares.
* Canadian brewer Molson Cos. Ltd. class A sank 0.60 to 19.50, a 52-week low, on 1.3 million shares.
* Trizec Corp. Ltd. topped the volume list, edging up 0.10 to 12.35 on 1.6 million shares.
* Biovail Corp. International jumped 3.80 to 49.80 on news that its new hypertension drug has captured a stronger share of doctors' prescriptions.
